default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1108.title: Bollinger squeeze release follow
E-1108.hypothesis: After bandwidth hits its lowest of the lookback, resting orders on both sides are stacked; the first close outside the band releases the compressed range in that direction.

E-1109.title: Bollinger band re-entry fade
E-1109.hypothesis: A close beyond k standard deviations is an overshoot by impatient flow; the first close back inside the band shows the push is spent, so trade back toward the mean.

E-1110.title: Day-open reclaim
E-1110.hypothesis: The session open is the reference price for the day's participants; after trading on one side for a while, the first close back across it shifts the day's balance, so follow the cross.

E-1111.title: Clock-hour open reclaim
E-1111.hypothesis: Hourly candles are watched by many desks; after trading below/above the current hour's open, a close back across it marks a shift in that hour's control, so follow it.

E-1112.title: Autocorrelation regime switch
E-1112.hypothesis: When the recent lag-1 return autocorrelation is strongly negative the market is bouncing (fade the last bar); when strongly positive it is trending in small steps (follow it).

E-1113.title: Index and dollar moving together: fade
E-1113.hypothesis: WIN and WDO normally move in opposite directions; a large simultaneous same-direction move is an anomaly driven by one-sided flow in a thin market and tends to be reversed.

E-1114.title: Bar-gap continuation
E-1114.hypothesis: A bar opening far from the previous close, relative to the recent average range, shows an order burst between bars; if the bar then closes beyond the old close in the gap direction, follow.

E-1115.title: Seasonal minute drift
E-1115.hypothesis: Some clock times show a recurring one-way drift (scheduled flows, index rebalancing, data releases); trade the sign of the average forward return from this minute over the previous 20 sessions when it is consistent.

E-1116.title: Shock-bar failure
E-1116.hypothesis: A bar with a range far above the norm for its minute of day is a burst of aggressive orders; if the next bar closes back through the shock bar's midpoint, the burst is being absorbed, so trade against it.

E-1117.title: Prior-close reclaim
E-1117.hypothesis: The previous session's close is the settlement reference for overnight and gap positions; after trading on one side of it for a while, a close back across it signals gap holders giving up, so follow.
